The study is testing FAM-010 , a new investigational chemotherapy designed to be gentler on the heart. Your dog may be eligible if they recently had their spleen removed or have surgery scheduled. Contact the study team What is hemangiosarcoma? Hemangiosarcoma is an aggressive cancer that starts in the blood vessels, most often in the spleen. It often shows few signs until a tumor bleeds, so many dogs are diagnosed suddenly, sometimes in an emergency. Treatment usually starts with surgery to remove the spleen, followed by chemotherapy. Even with both, the cancer often comes back, and there is still no FDA-approved treatment for hemangiosarcoma in dogs. How is FAM-010 different? Doxorubicin is the current standard chemotherapy for dogs with hemangiosarcoma after surgery. But it can also reach and damage healthy tissues, especially the heart. This limits the total amount of chemotherapy a dog can receive. FAM-010 is a new form of doxorubicin, designed to carry more of the medicine to the cancer and less of it to the heart. We hope this will let dogs receive more of the treatment they need, more safely. What will this study tell us? This first study will find the right dose of FAM-010 for dogs: the highest dose they can receive without side effects becoming too much. Every dog in the study receives FAM-010, given as a short infusion every three weeks at the University of Illinois, and the study team monitors each dog closely throughout. FAM-010 is investigational and not approved by FDA for dogs. This study is designed to establish the dose and understand its side effects. STUDY ELIGIBILITY Could this study be an option for your dog? If the following apply to your dog, we encourage you to contact us. Our study team will review your dog’s medical history and test results to confirm eligibility. Diagnosis A pathology report has confirmed hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, or you are waiting for the result. Recent spleen surgery Your dog has had their spleen removed or has surgery scheduled. Timing You are able to travel to the study site in Urbana Illinois within 21 days after surgery. Previous treatment Your dog has not received chemotherapy, radiation or another investigational drug. Travel to Urbana, Illinois You could bring your dog to Urbana for regular study visits. Breeding Your dog is not intended for breeding. Wondering if your dog might qualify? Filling out the form doesn’t commit you to anything. Tell us a little about your dog, and if the study looks like a fit, we’ll connect you with the University of Illinois study team to confirm eligibility and answer your questions. Contact the study team Questions about the study A cancer diagnosis brings a lot of decisions at once. If your dog has been diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma, this study could give them access to a new investigational treatment at no cost to you, with close care from the veterinary team at the University of Illinois. Contact the study team Why might I consider this study for my dog? You may want to consider it if you and your veterinarian are looking at care options after hemangiosarcoma diagnosis and after spleen surgery. Your dog would receive the study drug and be monitored by the oncology team at Illinois, with study care paid for by Familiar.
